𝟯𝟬-year Treasury yield and its falling channel

𝟯𝟬-year yield: 𝟱.𝟲𝟰% on 𝟯𝟬 Sep 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲, +𝟯.𝟲𝟵 points versus the channel's upper line; +𝟭𝟬.𝟭 wide gaps from the center line.
It first closed a week above the 𝟭𝟵𝟴𝟳-𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟭 channel in Apr 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟮: the falling channel has not held since.
Yield change 𝟮𝟲 weeks after each trip beyond 𝟮 wide gaps: Aug 𝟭𝟵𝟵𝟬 +𝟮.𝟱: -𝟭.𝟭𝟬 pts, Oct 𝟭𝟵𝟵𝟯 -𝟯.𝟮: +𝟭.𝟱𝟭 pts, Nov 𝟭𝟵𝟵𝟰 +𝟮.𝟮: -𝟭.𝟭𝟰 pts, Oct 𝟭𝟵𝟵𝟴 -𝟯.𝟭: +𝟬.𝟳𝟰 pts, Jun 𝟮𝟬𝟬𝟯 -𝟮.𝟬: +𝟬.𝟴𝟭 pts, Dec 𝟮𝟬𝟬𝟴 -𝟯.𝟲: +𝟭.𝟵𝟳 pts, Jun 𝟮𝟬𝟭𝟮 -𝟮.𝟮: +𝟬.𝟮𝟴 pts, Nov 𝟮𝟬𝟭𝟴 +𝟮.𝟰: -𝟬.𝟱𝟯 pts.

Above the 𝟭𝟵𝟴𝟳-𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟭 falling channel at 𝟱.𝟲𝟰%: the old channel no longer holds.

The 𝟯𝟬-year yield closed at 𝟱.𝟲𝟰%, 𝟭𝟬.𝟭 wide gaps above the center of a channel that held from 𝟭𝟵𝟴𝟳 to 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟭. Past trips near 𝟮 gaps reversed within 𝟮𝟲 weeks; this break has held since 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟮, so homebuilders never get cheaper mortgages. I own cash and short homebuilders, and a weekly close back inside the 𝟭𝟵𝟴𝟳-𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟭 channel proves me wrong.
